chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man whose ablution breaks after he raises his head from the last prostration, before he performs the Tashahhud, he said: He should leave and perform ablution. So if he wishes, he returns to the mosque, and if he wishes, [he does so] in his house, and if he wishes, wherever he wishes. He sits and performs the Tashahhud, then gives the greeting. And if the breaking of ablution occurred after the Tashahhud, then his prayer has passed (is completed).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person's ablution breaks after the last prostration but before the final greeting in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the transitional state of the prayer, distinguishing between the period after the final prostration but before the final sitting as incomplete, thereby necessitating a renewal of ablution without invalidating the prayer itself. The ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the worshipper to complete the ritual in any location, which underscores the practical ease (rukhas) granted to believers in maintaining ritual purity. This specific scenario is often contrasted with breaking ablution after the final sitting, where the prayer is considered fully concluded and no further action is required.
